summary: Independent basic-depth functional review of commit f037bd977817c78940457146b6836330e6f1b746 against base 337d3999d5f1113752873b129a52f95aae6623ba found no functional defects. Reviewed every changed hunk and both attached PNG assets, with adjacent welcome rendering, resident routing, static versioning, MIME and package-data behavior.

changed_files.lines_changed: Date updated; browser icon and serving behavior documented.
Resident PNG added to shared static assets.
Resident PNG registered through the packaged shared web directory.
New binary PNG; inspected the attached white-on-black circled Z.
New binary PNG; inspected the attached black-on-white circled Z.
Employee PNG added to cached media replacement pairs.
Anonymous inline favicon and protected authenticated PNG behavior asserted.
Favicon parsing, bytes, MIME, versioning and packaging assertions added across nine entry paths.

positive_changes: Welcome rendering replaces the favicon marker with a PNG data URI through the existing cached media path. The employee CSP already permits data images, and anonymous asset permissions remain unchanged.

Both resident registrations resolve to the shared packaged resident PNG. Existing host, expiry and request-method handling remains ahead of or around static serving; no resident data route is introduced.

StaticAssets includes the new PNG bytes in its release digest and rewrites registered HTML favicon links with the current version. PNG responses use image/png, existing conditional GET/HEAD handling and existing version-sensitive cache policies.

The existing zava_forward.api web/* package-data pattern includes both PNGs. The Docker build copies API sources and installs the resulting wheel; the preview's relative asset path resolves within the installed package layout.
The supplied validation evidence reports focused test, lint, format, type and headed Chromium favicon checks passing. Those checks were not rerun during this read-only review.
risk_assessment: Low: isolated static branding and media registration using existing serving mechanisms. No tests, network calls, Git mutations or private dataset reads were performed. Concurrent paper PDF/TeX edits and unrelated source changes were excluded.
